hypotheses.title: Single-field record member type lookup is O(N) in the record's field count (linear scans and per-comparison allocations in semtypes), so code touching all fields of a wide record is O(N^2)
hypotheses.issue: Every field access r.fK / self.fK and every field of a mapping constructor checked against a record type asks semtypes for a member type with a singleton string key, and each such lookup did O(N) work in the number of fields N of the record atom. (1) semtypes/mapping_ops.go mappingAtomicApplicableMemberTypesInner (and its duplicate mappingAtomicApplicableMemberTypesInnerProj in mapping_proj.go) called cellInner() on ALL N field cells into an unsized slice, although only the matching index was used. It also received MappingAtomicType by value. (2) getStringSubtypeListCoverage -> stringListIntersect (semtypes/string_ops.go) merge-walked all N sorted names instead of binary-searching, and (3) heap-allocated two enumerableString values via enumerableStringFrom for each comparison step. (4) MappingAtomicType.FieldCell / FieldInnerVal / IsOptional and mappingAtomHasFieldByName / mappingAtomHasOptionalFieldByName (semtypes/mapping_atomic_type.go) scan m.names linearly. They are called once per field from mapping-constructor checking (type_resolver.go resolveMappingConstructorFields/finishMappingConstructor, analysis/constructors.go validateMappingConstructor) and from field access. On main with N=4000 the lookup function was ~44% of CPU and 95% of all allocated bytes (1.87 of 1.98 GB); most of the remaining CPU was GC caused by those allocations. Each doubling of N cost about 3-4x more time.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate wide_record_<N>.bal: a closed record with N fields, read field-by-field.

Every `r.fK` field access (and every field of the mapping constructor) asks
semtypes for the member type of a singleton string key. That lookup walks /
materialises all N fields of the record atom, so a function touching all N
fields costs O(N^2).
Usage: gen.py N [ACCESSES]   (ACCESSES defaults to N)
"""
import sys
n = int(sys.argv[1])
acc = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else n
out = ["import ballerina/io;\n\n", "type Wide record {|\n"]
out += [f"    int f{i};\n" for i in range(n)]
out.append("|};\n\n")
out.append("function make() returns Wide {\n    return {")
out.append(", ".join(f"f{i}: {i}" for i in range(n)))
out.append("};\n}\n\n")
out.append("function sumFields(Wide r) returns int {\n    int s = 0;\n")
out += [f"    s += r.f{i % n};\n" for i in range(acc)]
out.append("    return s;\n}\n\n")
out.append("public function main() {\n    io:println(sumFields(make()));\n}\n")
open(f"/tmp/perfhunt/H1/wide_record_{n}" + (f"_{acc}" if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "") + ".bal", "w").write("".join(out))

python3 gen.py 8000  # writes /tmp/perfhunt/H1/wide_record_8000.bal

hypotheses.fix_approach: Two steps, both inside semtypes. (1) Make the singleton-key member lookup proportional to the number of matched keys rather than to N. mappingAtomicApplicableMemberTypesInner takes *MappingAtomicType and calls cellInner only on the matched indices (and on rest only when needed), with pre-sized result slices. The duplicate *Proj variant in mapping_proj.go is deleted in favour of the shared function. stringListIntersect does a binary search (sort.SearchStrings) per target key over the sorted names instead of a merge walk that allocates enumerableString values per comparison. (2) Add a private MappingAtomicType.fieldIndex(name) using slices.BinarySearch(m.names, name), and use it in FieldCell, IsOptional, mappingAtomHasFieldByName and mappingAtomHasOptionalFieldByName instead of linear scans. Correctness relies on MappingAtomicType.names always being sorted. I checked every constructor: splitFields sorts, the predefined atoms (kind/value/visibility, $qualifiers) are written in sorted order, insertField does a sorted insert using codePointCompare, intersectMapping uses newFieldPairs (sorted merge), and the old merge walk already assumed sorted input. Code-point order equals Go byte order for valid UTF-8, and the old comparator was plain Go string <. Pitfall: after step 1 alone, N=4000 looks fixed (the profile becomes flat), but the FieldCell linear scan is still quadratic and only shows at N>=8000-16000. Measurement note: at N=4000 the fixed run takes ~260 ms and the benchmark tool flagged its CV (5.4-10.7%) as unreliable on 3 separate runs, so N=8000 was used for the pass criterion. `make test` passed after each attempt.

notes: Attempt 1 (singleton-key lookup + binary search in stringListIntersect) already gave -81% time on N=4000, but the benchmark tool flagged the time as unreliable (CV 9.9% / 6.6%), so attempt 2 was spawned on top of it and also removed the remaining O(N) FieldCell scan. Prototype commits stay local on claude/perf-20261027-H1 (not pushed).
